image_description: A medium shot of a person wearing a yellow academic gown with black velvet panels and a black mortarboard cap. The subject is holding a white diploma cover. The background shows other graduates in similar attire, suggesting an outdoor commencement ceremony.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flowing full-length garment with rectangular silhouette draping from shoulders to ankles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped at the waist/hip level; the lower half of the gown and ankles are not visible.
The gown exhibits clear bilateral symmetry with a distinct vertical opening down the center front, revealing the white shirt underneath.
The fabric hangs loosely and does not cling to the torso or arms, successfully obscuring the underlying body shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide open sleeves extending well below hand level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The sleeve on the subject's left arm is clearly visible as a wide, bell-shaped extension that hangs significantly past the wrist/hand area.
Distinct black vertical panels (likely velvet) run along the front edges of the yellow gown, serving as the visual closure elements.
A white collared dress shirt is clearly visible beneath the open front of the gown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the color is yellow (not black), the fabric exhibits a heavy, opaque, and matte finish consistent with traditional gown materials like polyester or gabardine.
The fabric surface is smooth and absorbs light rather than reflecting it sharply, indicating a non-reflective finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drape of the sleeve fabric follows gravity naturally and extends visibly beyond the subject's wrist line.

Structural integrity of the diploma cover
